text:
maya: Heads-up — after the reconnect-backoff rollout we just flipped, console shows a ~2x spike in active sessions for a handful of tenants. Not seeing corresponding increases in backend accepts. Anyone else seeing duplicate session IDs in logs?

sam: saw the alert. can you paste a sample log line?

maya: yup — from edge-proxy: `2024-05-03T12:34:10Z INFO RESUME token=abc123 session_id=sess-7f4e backend_accept=false backoff_ms=800` then 250ms later another: `RESUME token=abc123 session_id=sess-7f4e backend_accept=true`

josh: that pattern suggests client retried while the proxy was still reconciling resume state. The backoff jitter we pushed is non-deterministic, so duplicate session counter increments when the console sampling aggregates by accept events.

elaine: console-team here — the dashboard increments "active_sessions" from the stream-accept metric emitted by the ingress. We also do a sampling normalization which changed in the same deploy (sampling_fraction moved from 0.1 -> 0.25). Could be two independent changes colliding.

ops-bot: alert: tenant=acct-42 active_session_spike > 150% for 3m — triggered at 2024-05-03T12:36:05Z

sam: ah ok. so symptoms = console shows 2x, backend traces show single accepted connection. Is this just a telemetry duplication issue or are we actually double-billing?

maya: quick check of billing pipeline shows token-usage counters did NOT double for these tenants. so far looks like telemetry/stats duplication, not billing. but UX panic is real.

josh: possible explanation: ingress increments metric on resume START and again on resume COMPLETE, but console aliasing expects only COMPLETE. With the higher sampling fraction, more STARTs surface in aggregates. Previously those START events were mostly dropped.

elaine: can we change console to only count `stream_accept==true` events? Right now we count both `stream_resume_started` and `stream_resume_completed` and dedupe later, but dedupe depends on session fingerprinting which fails when session_id rounds trip through opaque proxy.

sam: quick mitigation: revert sampling_fraction to 0.1 and flip the resume-start increment to be gated by `backend_accept==true`. Will that be safe to hotfix?

maya: yeah, we can hotfix ingress to not emit `stream_resume_started` metric until we see backend_accept. patch ready: `diff -- ingress/handler.go +3 -1` snippet: ```
if backendAccept {
  emitMetric("stream_resume_completed")
} else {
  // hold off on counting until accept
}
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued for team=ingress, env=staging, pr=#PLAT-4321

josh: long term we should: 1) make session fingerprints stable across proxy hops, 2) revise console dedupe to use fingerprint rather than session_id, 3) add a small TTL window for counting resume events (e.g., 1s) to collapse rapid retries.

elaine: agreed. filing follow-ups: PLAT-4322 (fingerprint fix), PLAT-4323 (console dedupe by fingerprint), PLAT-4324 (resume-ttl collapse). I'll also add a note in the rollout doc to avoid sampling + metric schema changes in the same push.

maya: rolling the sampling_fraction revert now. will monitor dashboards. if we still see spikes after revert we escalate.

ops-bot: incident-note: mitigation applied (sampling revert) at 2024-05-03T12:44:10Z.

sam: thanks. quick telemetry ask: can eng-platform add a short-lived synthetic that exercises resume start/complete paths and emits trace-id so console shows end-to-end? would speed debugging in future.

maya: good idea — I'll add a smoke probe to the canary job.

console-team: FYI we'll mute pager for these tenant spikes while mitigation runs and watch the follow-ups. :thumbsup:

maya: if mitigation looks stable we'll still keep the follow-ups prioritized before the next rollout. thx all.
